textRuns.value: 1. Sample ratio mismatch (SRM): a chi-square test of the treated/control counts against an expected 50/50 split. A p-value above 0.01 means group sizes are consistent with random assignment.

2. Covariate balance: if assignment was random, pre-campaign behaviour (spend, points, products) should look the same in both groups. The standardized mean difference (SMD) is the gap between group means in standard-deviation units; below 0.1 is conventionally balanced. It is preferred over p-values here because very large samples make tiny, harmless differences look significant.

Limits: balance is tested on all 200,039 campaign clients - pre-campaign purchase history plus age and gender from clients.csv (ages outside 14-99 treated as missing). Region is not in the data. Passing these checks supports, but does not prove, random assignment.
